images.caption: First Lutheran Church in downtown Moline, Illinois.

brief: Big Gothic Revival red-brick church of 1876 in the downtown of a factory city: a tall central front tower with a clock stage, pinnacles and a spire, buff-brick pointed-arch trim, buttressed side walls and a stone name panel reading its founding year.

facade.notes: First Evangelical Lutheran (Moline IL, 1876): a red-brick Gothic Revival church with cream stone trim, a tall central front tower with a clock stage, pinnacles and a parapet, buttressed side walls with tall pointed windows; a new parking lot alongside -- a Swedish immigrant congregation's church

why.note: a church is a long nave pointed at the street with a tower marking the entrance
the Gothic Revival as the default church style of the late 1800s
